overall: The Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when a quorum deliberated outside a posted meeting by text on March 27 and April 30; no violation on the April 28 meeting; additional allegations declined. Compliance ordered, no further remedy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged three councilors on the zoning committee deliberated on short-term rental rules by text and email outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Councilors Schnepp, Cullum, and Beedenbender improperly deliberated via text message on March 27 and April 30.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged two councilors used FaceTime and texts to circumvent the Open Meeting Law for the April 28 meeting, letting a quorum participate without notice.
allegations.key_passage: we lack specific evidence that Councilors Cullum and Beedenbender did, in fact, engage in serial communication

allegations.summary: Request for further review raised additional allegations not included in the formal complaint filed with the Committee.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the additional allegations raised in the request for further review and subsequent communications with our office because they were not raised in a formal Open Meeting Law complaint filed with the Board.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
